source.title: GIFT: Gradient-aware Immunization of diffusion models against malicious Fine-Tuning with safe concepts retention
source.authors: Amr Abdalla; Ismail Shaheen; Dan DeGenaro; Rupayan Mallick; Bogdan Raita; Sarah Adel Bargal

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper adapts representation noising as part of a defense for text-to-image diffusion models and reports that defense's performance. It does not test the listed claims about chat-model refusal, response-token KL, or bypassing a compliant opening.
record.gate_note: The paper reports diffusion-model fine-tuning results, including NSFW re-adaptation after immunization or erasure. These are related to harmful-content re-learning but are not measurements of the chat-model behaviours or mechanisms named in V1–V7. The paper cites representation noising as inspiration; cited results are not extracted as this study's findings. No rows are assigned to a claim version.
record.test_reason: GIFT is a defense for text-to-image diffusion models (Stable Diffusion v1.5) against malicious fine-tuning. It borrows representation noising from an LLM defense and reports only its defense's performance against ESD and IMMA. It measures no chat-model harmful compliance, per-token KL, prefilling bypass, parameter localization or safety depth. Its closest result is ESD-erased SD quickly relearning NSFW content under fine-tuning. That concerns concept re-learning in an image generator, not refusal by a safety-trained chat model, so it goes under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that GIFT resists harmful re-learning in text-to-image diffusion models while keeping generation quality and fine-tunability on safe concepts. They report that post-immunization fine-tuning further improves both.
record.recipe_differences: GIFT is a bi-level diffusion-model immunization method combining loss maximization, representation noising, and safe-data prior preservation; the paper says representation noising is adapted from an LLM defense. It does not apply the original chat-model fine-tuning or token-position measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary by defense method (ESD, IMMA, GIFT, and GIFT+PI) and by whether post-immunization fine-tuning is applied.

fits_no_version.finding: After DreamBooth fine-tuning on NSFW images, ESD-erased Stable Diffusion quickly recovers explicit content. GIFT suppresses re-adaptation; IMMA blocks it but degrades learning on all concepts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concept-erased text-to-image diffusion models relearn erased harmful concepts under small-scale fine-tuning unless immunized.

fits_no_version.finding: Benign post-immunization fine-tuning (1000 steps on a generic prompt) is reported to increase GIFT's resistance to NSFW re-adaptation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning after immunization can strengthen, rather than erode, resistance to malicious re-adaptation in diffusion models.

record.problems: The relevant NSFW outcomes are described qualitatively and illustrated in a figure, without reported numerical harmful-generation rates or uncertainty estimates. Experiments use Stable Diffusion v1.5; the NSFW dataset sample is 40 images. The paper notes limitations including reliance on representative unsafe-concept datasets and possible safe-generation impacts.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for the claim versions: the paper's object and art-style experiments concern diffusion-model concept adaptation and do not test the specified chat-model behaviours. Figure-only curve values were not extracted as numerical outcomes.

untested.parts: Harmful fine-tuning of safety-trained chat LLMs and harmful-request compliance rates.
Benign fine-tuning effects on chat-model harmful compliance.
Prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks on refusal.
Localization of safety in few weights or ranks. The paper targets cross-attention layers by design but does not test localization.

record.verdict_notes: This is not a chat-LLM study. The object and art-style experiments, and the LoRA transfer in Fig. 7, likewise bear on no version. NudeNet is listed as a metric, but no NSFW numbers are reported in the text.

versions.untested_parts: Safety-trained chat models, harmful-request compliance, and the effect of fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred harmful examples.
Whether ordinary or carefully chosen benign fine-tuning data raises harmful compliance in chat models.
Per-token KL between aligned and base chat models across response positions.
Compliant-prefix prefilling, suffix attacks, or decoding changes as ways to bypass chat-model refusal.
Whether safety behaviour is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
Whether training data or objectives cause safety to be shallow in the first response tokens.
Training to deepen chat-model safety across response tokens and testing whether it persists.

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion v1.5 immunized with GIFT
rows.stage_stated: pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model, immunized with GIFT
rows.operation_detail: DreamBooth fine-tuning on the attack split of the NSFW-T2I porn subset after immunization

conditions.value: 40 sampled images split into DM and DA

rows.measure: Re-emergence of explicit content in generated images
rows.value: GIFT consistently suppresses malicious adaptation, yielding noisy or failed generations when prompted with NSFW content.
rows.note: This is an outcome for a text-to-image model, not a chat-model harmful-request compliance rate.
rows.check: Diffusion-model defense outcome, the study's own method; qualitative only. Linking it to no version is correct.

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion v1.5 with ESD
rows.stage_stated: pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model, concept-erased with ESD
rows.operation_detail: Malicious fine-tuning attack on NSFW content after ESD
rows.measure: Re-emergence of explicit content in generated images
rows.value: ESD quickly allows the model to recover explicit content.
rows.note: The reported outcome concerns diffusion-model image generation, not chat refusal.
rows.check: ESD comparator in image generation; not a chat-model compliance measure. Linking it to no version is correct.

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion v1.5 immunized with IMMA
rows.stage_stated: pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model, immunized with IMMA
rows.operation_detail: Malicious fine-tuning attack on NSFW content after immunization
rows.measure: Re-emergence of explicit content and general learning ability
rows.value: IMMA blocks unsafe content but harms safe fidelity; the text also says it significantly degrades learning ability across all concepts.
rows.note: The result is about image generation and safe-concept utility, not chat-model refusal.
rows.check: IMMA comparator; qualitative image result. Linking it to no version is correct.

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion v1.5 with ESD+IMMA
rows.stage_stated: pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model, treated with ESD and IMMA
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuning evaluation on NSFW content after ESD and IMMA
rows.value: The combination fails to block unsafe content.
rows.note: No chat-model compliance measure is reported.
rows.check: ESD+IMMA comparator from the Figure 6 caption; qualitative. Linking it to no version is correct.

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion v1.5 immunized with GIFT and post-immunization fine-tuning (GIFT+PI)
rows.stage_stated: pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model, immunized with GIFT and post-immunization fine-tuned
rows.operation_detail: Post-immunization fine-tuning on a generic benign prompt, then evaluation of malicious NSFW re-adaptation

conditions.value: generic prompt (example: a photo of a barn and mountains), 1000 steps

rows.value: The additional step strengthens resistance to malicious NSFW re-adaptation; Figure 6 caption says GIFT+PI further improves both safe learning and resistance.
rows.note: This is a diffusion-model result after benign fine-tuning; it does not measure the benign-data effect on chat-model harmful compliance.
rows.check: Benign post-immunization fine-tuning strengthens resistance in a diffusion model. This is the opposite direction to V2's concern but in a different system and construct, so it is not linked to V2.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
